title: Let’s run Julia everywhere from mobile to web
text:
What I created

SubsetJuliaVM (a.k.a sjulia)

Supports a subset of Julia’s syntax
A stack-based VM (Virtual Machine) implemented in Rust

Runs on iOS and Android devices

The VM compiles to WebAssembly, so it also runs in the browser

Supports parts of Plots.jl, OrdinaryDiffEq.jl, AbstractAlgebra.jl, and more

title: Let’s run Julia everywhere from mobile to web
text:
Why I created it

I wanted to run Julia on my iPad.

iOS / iPadOS (no JIT allowed, strict App Store review)
W^X (Write XOR Execute) policy

What about Binder or Google Colab?

Unusable where the internet connection is unreliable
Installing external packages takes a long time

title: Let’s run Julia everywhere from mobile to web
text:
How I created it

Apps like Pythonista and Carnets do run on iOS.

So why not build a virtual machine that accepts Julia syntax?!

Let’s actually build it!

A stack-based bytecode interpreter (no JIT)
Julia source → Parser → Lowering → Compiler → VM
Built with heavy use of AI tools: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi, etc.
Result: AtelierArith/julia-vm-oss

title: Let’s run Julia everywhere from mobile to web
section: How sjulia differs from upstream Julia
text:
How sjulia differs from upstream Julia
How code is interpreted and executed:








Stage
Upstream Julia
SubsetJuliaVM




Parser
flisp / JuliaSyntax.jl
pure Rust parser → CST


Lowering
lowered IR
Rust implementation → Core IR


Code generation
native code via LLVM JIT at runtime
bytecode compiler (done before execution)


Execution
native code
stack-based VM (bytecode interpretation)


Runtime
C runtime + pure Julia base/
Rust builtins + a pure Julia subset




With no JIT, SubsetJuliaVM runs even on iOS (W^X) and WASM

Performance: Julia vs. SubsetJuliaVM
Mandelbrot set benchmark (Apple Silicon macOS, measured 2026-07):


function mandel_point(c::ComplexF64,
                      maxiter::Int64)::Int64
    z = 0.0 + 0.0im
    for k in 1:maxiter
        abs2(z) > 4.0 && return k - 1
        z = z * z + c
    end
    return maxiter
end

function mandel_count(width, height, maxiter)
    total = 0
    for y in 1:height
        ci = -1.2 + 2.4 * (y - 1) / (height - 1)
        for x in 1:width
            cr = -2.0 + 3.0 * (x - 1) / (width - 1)
            total += mandel_point(cr + ci * im, maxiter)
        end
    end
    total
end

mandel_count(1500, 1500, 500)  # same source for all implementations

title: Let’s run Julia everywhere from mobile to web
text:
This webpage serves as a repository for the presentation materials and links I will be discussing at JuliaCon 2026.

Slide

We implemented a Rust-based virtual machine that accepts and executes a subset of Julia syntax. This enables Julia code to run in environments where the official runtime is difficult to deploy. By compiling the VM to WebAssembly, Julia can run web apps for educational purposes, and static linking with Swift or Flutter allows mobile applications. This short talk demonstrates these capabilities through live demos.
